title: Observation siphon: per-tenant credit pools and budgeted sampling for non-blocking mirroring
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Build a non-blocking observation pipeline ("siphon") that duplicates a configurable fraction of live inference traffic for downstream evaluation without affecting production latency or cost budgets. The siphon must provide per-tenant accounting, dynamic budgeted sampling, and strong provenance so mirrored requests are traceable and billable to a tenant-specific credit pool.

Scope: gateway-side duplication with an async sidecar writer, tenant-scoped credit pools, a dynamic sampler that adjusts to global and per-tenant budgets, tagging/provenance headers for downstream evaluators, and a fail-safe that disables mirroring for a tenant when budget is exhausted. Not included: full end-to-end A/B orchestration (separate ticket).

Success metrics: 1) Production p99 latency increase <= 0.5ms attributable to siphon under 95th percentile load. 2) Mirrored QPS sustained with <2% request loss under normal conditions. 3) Per-tenant spend adherence: mirrored cost charged to tenant credit pool with <=1% accounting drift. 4) Ability to flexibly scale sampling rate per tenant in <2 minutes from console change.

Design highlights and trade-offs: 1) Asynchronous duplication: we chose an async sidecar writer pattern (gateway enqueues a lightweight observation message) over in-line duplication to guarantee zero blocking on the main request path. Trade-off: eventual consistency for mirror delivery, but deterministic lower tail latency. 2) Credit-based sampler: each tenant has a credit pool (monthly or contractual). The sampler enforces a dynamic sampling rate so consumption stays within the credit envelope. We will use an exponentially-weighted short-term estimator of consumption and backfill credits with burst tokens. 3) Sampling algorithm: token-cost aware reservoir sampler (tokens ~ expected decoder tokens) rather than uniform sampling, reducing cost while preserving signal for large responses. 4) Isolation: mirrored requests are routed to isolated evaluation clusters (canary/dedicated) with tenant-aware network tags and strict RBAC so customer data never escapes allowed boundaries. 5) Fail-safes: cascading disablement (per-tenant -> per-region -> global) and circuit-breaker metrics exposed as console alerts.

Integration with canary/rollback flow: mirrored outputs are compared to baseline model outputs using an offline evaluator. A drift monitor aggregates deltas and, when thresholds exceeded for a configured window, will surface a rollout advisory. We are NOT yet enabling automated rollback directly from mirrored drift signals; instead, the pipeline will create a high-priority alert and a pre-populated rollback runbook/APIs for manual or semi-automatic action (follow-up ticket to add auto-rollback).

Telemetry & billing: mirrored events will contain provenance headers (X-RW-Obs-Id, X-RW-Model-Version, X-RW-Sample-Score) and will be emitted to an observability topic with tenant tags for downstream billing pipelines. We will emit accounting flushes every 60s per tenant to reduce drift while keeping write amplification reasonable.

Operational considerations: - Backpressure: enqueue depth limits and admission control to protect gateway memory. - Cost fencing: per-tenant soft and hard thresholds; hard threshold disables mirroring immediately with a notification. - Privacy: redaction hooks in sidecar to remove sensitive fields before persistence if required by customer policy. - Testing: load tests will run with synthetic tenants (3x, 10x normal traffic) and fault injection for sidecar failures.

Deliverables: design doc, sidecar implementation, gateway hook, dynamic sampling service, console controls (sampling slider, credit top-up), dashboards (per-tenant spend, delivery success, latency delta), and a rollout plan for opt-in customer pilots.
